# Robot System for Versatile Article Handling

## Overview

The proposed robot system offers a highly efficient and flexible solution for handling a wide variety of articles by leveraging a minimal set of pre-registered reference articles. Rather than requiring exhaustive, item-specific programming for every conceivable object the robot might encounter, this system is designed to generalize from a small library of known references, dramatically reducing the setup and configuration burden typically associated with robotic manipulation tasks.

## Handling Unknown Articles Through Shape Similarity

One of the key strengths of this system lies in its ability to manipulate articles that have not been explicitly registered beforehand. As long as an unknown article's shape closely resembles that of one of the pre-registered reference articles, the system can successfully identify an appropriate handling strategy and execute the necessary manipulation. This shape-based generalization capability allows the robot to adapt to real-world variability in object dimensions, contours, and geometry without necessitating constant reprogramming or manual intervention, making the system well-suited for dynamic environments where the exact inventory of articles may not be fully known in advance.

## System Architecture

To achieve this flexible handling capability, the system is composed of several key functional units that work in concert:

### Mechanism Unit

The mechanism unit serves as the physical actuator of the system, responsible for directly interacting with and manipulating the target article. This unit executes the mechanical actions—such as gripping, lifting, rotating, or repositioning—that are necessary to handle the article according to the operation method determined by the system.

### Shape Measurement Unit

The shape measurement unit is tasked with capturing and analyzing the geometric characteristics of the article to be manipulated. By measuring the shape of the target object, this unit provides critical input data that allows the system to compare the unknown article against the pre-registered reference articles and determine the degree of similarity between them.

### Operation Method Calculation Unit

At the core of the system's adaptive capability is the operation method calculation unit. This unit takes the shape data obtained from the shape measurement unit and uses it to appropriately deform or adjust a set of stored basic operations—predefined manipulation templates associated with the reference articles. Through this deformation process, the unit generates a customized operation method tailored to the specific shape characteristics of the article at hand, even if that article was not explicitly pre-registered in the system.

### Control Unit

Once the operation method calculation unit has generated the suitable operation method, the control unit takes over to translate this method into actionable commands. The control unit directs the mechanism unit, ensuring that the physical actions performed align precisely with the calculated operation method, thereby completing the manipulation task effectively and accurately.

## Conclusion

By integrating shape measurement, adaptive operation calculation, and precise mechanical control, this robot system achieves a high degree of versatility in article handling while minimizing the need for extensive pre-registration of every possible object. This approach not only streamlines system deployment but also enhances the robot's capacity to respond intelligently to novel articles encountered during operation.

# Robot System for Handling Diverse Articles with Minimal Pre-Registration

## Background and Technical Challenge

Industrial and service robots are increasingly required to handle a wide variety of articles in real-world environments—from manufacturing components to household objects. Traditional robotic manipulation systems rely heavily on extensive databases of pre-registered articles, where each object's shape, grasping points, and manipulation sequence must be individually programmed and stored before the robot can interact with it. This approach, while effective for controlled environments with limited object variety, becomes impractical when robots must handle numerous articles with subtle variations in shape, size, or configuration.

The fundamental challenge lies in the trade-off between registration effort and operational flexibility. Registering every possible article variant demands substantial time, computational resources, and manual effort from system operators. Furthermore, in dynamic environments where new articles are frequently introduced, maintaining an exhaustive registration database becomes increasingly burdensome and unsustainable. This limitation has historically restricted the practical deployment of robotic systems to environments with highly standardized, unchanging article sets.

## System Architecture

To address these limitations, the present robot system introduces an innovative architecture comprising three core components that work in concert to enable flexible article handling with minimal pre-registration requirements.

### Mechanism Unit

The mechanism unit serves as the physical manipulation apparatus of the robot system, encompassing the robotic arm, end effector (such as grippers, suction devices, or specialized tools), and associated actuators. This unit executes the physical movements required to grasp, lift, reposition, or otherwise manipulate target articles based on commands derived from the system's processing units. The mechanism unit is designed with sufficient degrees of freedom and precision to accommodate the range of adjusted operations that the system may generate.

### Shape Measurement Unit

The shape measurement unit is responsible for capturing real-time geometric information about the article currently presented to the robot system. Utilizing sensors such as 3D cameras, laser scanners, or structured light projection systems, this unit generates a detailed shape profile of the unknown or target article. This measured shape data serves as the critical input that enables the system to compare the current article against previously registered examples and subsequently calculate appropriate manipulation adjustments.

### Basic Operation Storage

The basic operation storage functions as a repository containing manipulation patterns—referred to as "basic operations"—for a limited set of known, pre-registered articles. Rather than storing exhaustive variations for every conceivable article, this storage unit maintains fundamental operational templates that capture the essential grasping points, movement trajectories, force parameters, and sequencing information necessary to successfully manipulate each registered article type. These stored patterns serve as foundational references rather than rigid, singular solutions.

## Operation Method Calculation Unit: The Core Innovation

The defining feature of this robot system is the operation method calculation unit, which bridges the gap between limited pre-registered data and the practical need to handle diverse, previously unseen articles. This unit performs the following critical functions:

1. **Shape Comparison**: The calculation unit compares the shape data obtained from the shape measurement unit against the shapes associated with articles in the basic operation storage, identifying registered articles with sufficient geometric similarity to the currently presented unknown article.

2. **Deformation and Adaptation**: Once a similar registered article is identified, the operation method calculation unit does not simply apply the stored basic operation verbatim. Instead, it intelligently deforms and adjusts the stored operation parameters—such as grasp points, approach angles, applied forces, and movement paths—to account for the specific dimensional and geometric differences between the registered article and the actual unknown article being handled.

3. **Operation Generation**: Through this deformation process, the unit generates a customized, executable operation method tailored specifically to the unknown article's actual measured shape, effectively extrapolating from known solutions to address novel situations.

## Practical Advantages and Applications

This architecture delivers substantial practical benefits over conventional robotic manipulation systems:

**Reduced Registration Burden**: Because the system can handle articles that merely resemble registered examples—rather than requiring exact matches—operators need only register a representative subset of articles rather than every possible variant. This dramatically reduces the setup time and computational resources required for system deployment.

**Enhanced Flexibility**: The system's ability to deform basic operations based on measured shape allows it to gracefully handle natural variations that commonly occur in real-world articles, such as manufacturing tolerances, packaging differences, or organic material variability.

**Scalability**: As the diversity of articles a robot system encounters grows, this approach scales more efficiently than traditional exhaustive-registration methods, since a single registered article can effectively serve as a template for an entire family of similar articles.

**Reduced Maintenance**: The system requires less frequent updates to its registration database, as newly encountered articles that fall within the similarity threshold of existing registered articles can be handled automatically without manual intervention.

## Conclusion

By integrating a mechanism unit, shape measurement unit, and basic operation storage with an intelligent operation method calculation unit capable of deforming stored operations based on real-time shape measurements, this robot system successfully addresses the longstanding challenge of balancing registration effort against operational flexibility. The system's capacity to manipulate unknown articles that closely resemble registered examples—without requiring individual pre-registration for each variant—significantly expands its practical applicability across diverse industrial and commercial settings, offering a more scalable and efficient solution for automated article handling.

# Robot Systems: An Overview

A robot system is an integrated combination of mechanical, electrical, and computational components designed to perform tasks autonomously or semi-autonomously, often replicating or augmenting human capabilities in various environments. These systems have become increasingly prevalent across industries, transforming manufacturing, healthcare, exploration, and everyday life.

## Core Components

At its foundation, a robot system typically consists of several essential elements:

**Sensors** serve as the system's perceptual interface with the environment, gathering data through cameras, lidar, ultrasonic detectors, or tactile sensors. This information allows the robot to understand its surroundings and make informed decisions.

**Actuators** provide the physical means of movement and interaction, converting electrical signals into mechanical motion through motors, hydraulics, or pneumatic systems. These components enable robots to manipulate objects, navigate spaces, or perform precise tasks.

**Controllers** function as the "brain" of the system, processing sensor data and generating appropriate commands for actuators. Modern controllers often incorporate microprocessors running sophisticated algorithms, including machine learning models that enable adaptive behavior.

**Power supplies** ensure sustained operation, whether through batteries for mobile robots or direct electrical connections for stationary industrial units.

## Classification and Applications

Robot systems can be categorized by their operational domain and level of autonomy. Industrial robots dominate manufacturing settings, performing repetitive tasks like welding, assembly, and packaging with high precision and speed. Service robots assist in domestic or commercial environments, ranging from vacuum cleaners to hospital delivery systems.

Autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) navigate dynamic environments using advanced mapping and localization techniques, finding applications in warehouses, agriculture, and search-and-rescue operations. Collaborative robots, or "cobots," are designed to work safely alongside humans, incorporating force-limiting technology and intuitive programming interfaces.

## Integration and Control Architecture

Effective robot systems require sophisticated software architectures that coordinate multiple subsystems simultaneously. This includes:

- Real-time operating systems for time-critical operations
- Communication protocols enabling coordination between multiple robots or components
- Feedback control loops that continuously adjust behavior based on sensor input
- Path planning and obstacle avoidance algorithms

## Future Directions

The evolution of robot systems continues to accelerate, driven by advances in artificial intelligence, materials science, and computing power. Emerging trends include swarm robotics, where multiple simple robots coordinate to accomplish complex tasks, and soft robotics, which utilizes flexible materials to enable safer human-robot interaction.

As these systems become more sophisticated, considerations around safety, ethics, and human-robot collaboration remain paramount. The integration of robot systems into society requires careful attention to reliability, transparency, and the preservation of human agency in increasingly automated environments.

Robot systems represent a convergence of multiple engineering disciplines, and their continued development promises to reshape how humans interact with technology and perform work across virtually every sector of the economy.

# Patent Abstract

**ROBOTIC MANIPULATION SYSTEM WITH SHAPE-ADAPTIVE MOTION GENERATION**

A robotic manipulation system and method for handling previously unencountered objects by adapting pre-registered basic motion patterns based on measured object shape data. The system includes a shape measurement unit configured to acquire three-dimensional shape data of a target object using one or more sensors, such as cameras, depth sensors, or laser scanners. A motion database stores a plurality of basic motion patterns, each associated with reference shape parameters corresponding to representative object categories or prototype shapes for which the motions were originally designed or taught.

Upon detecting a new object, a shape comparison unit analyzes the measured shape data against the reference shape parameters stored in the motion database to identify a basic motion pattern exhibiting the closest structural or geometric similarity to the target object. A motion adaptation unit then modifies the selected basic motion pattern by calculating correction parameters—including adjustments to gripping position, approach angle, grasping width, contact points, and trajectory waypoints—based on differences between the measured shape data and the reference shape parameters associated with the selected motion.

The adapted motion is executed by a robot arm and end effector to perform the manipulation task, such as grasping, lifting, or repositioning the object. A control unit oversees the overall operation, including real-time verification of task execution and, optionally, feedback-based refinement of the adaptation parameters if sensor feedback during execution indicates deviation from expected contact or force profiles. The system further allows for the newly adapted motion, together with its associated shape data, to be registered into the motion database as an additional entry, thereby expanding the library of usable motion patterns over time.

This configuration enables a robot to flexibly handle diverse and previously unregistered objects without requiring individualized motion programming for each new shape, thereby improving versatility, reducing setup time, and enhancing operational efficiency in applications such as logistics, manufacturing, and warehouse automation.

counterfactuals.output:
# PATENT APPLICATION

## TITLE OF THE INVENTION
**ROBOT SYSTEM AND METHOD FOR CALCULATING OPERATION BY DEFORMING BASIC MOTION DATA BASED ON MEASURED SHAPE OF UNKNOWN ARTICLE**

---

## TECHNICAL FIELD

[0001] The present disclosure relates to a robot system configured to handle articles, and more particularly, to a robot system and a control method thereof capable of generating an operation for an article whose shape is not registered in advance, by measuring the shape of the article and deforming previously stored basic operation data in accordance with the measured shape.

---

## BACKGROUND ART

[0002] Conventionally, robots used in factories, warehouses, and distribution centers have been configured to grip, convey, and place articles based on operation programs created in advance for known articles having predetermined shapes and dimensions. In such systems, when an unknown article whose shape has not been registered is to be handled, it has been necessary either to newly teach an operation for the unknown article through a teaching operation performed by an operator, or to prepare in advance operation data corresponding to every conceivable shape.

[0003] However, the teaching operation requires significant time and labor, and it is difficult to prepare operation data in advance for all shapes that a robot may encounter in an actual working environment where diverse articles of unknown shape are handled. Consequently, there is a demand for a technique enabling a robot to autonomously generate an appropriate operation for an unknown article without requiring a new teaching operation each time.

[0004] Further, even when an unknown article has a shape similar to that of an already known article, in the conventional art, since the unknown article is not identified as matching any registered shape, the robot operation corresponding to the known article cannot be utilized, and thus operation generation processing must be performed from the beginning, which is inefficient.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

### Problem to be Solved

[0005] An object of the present disclosure is to provide a robot system and a control method thereof capable of generating an appropriate robot operation for an unknown article, without requiring new teaching, by utilizing basic operation data prepared in advance for known articles and deforming such data in accordance with the actually measured shape of the unknown article.

### Means for Solving the Problem

[0006] In order to solve the above problem, a robot system according to an embodiment of the present disclosure includes:

a robot having an arm and an end effector attached to the arm and configured to act on an article;

a shape measurement unit configured to measure a shape of an article to be handled by the robot;

a storage unit configured to store, in advance, basic operation data indicating an operation of the robot for at least one basic article having a known shape; and

an operation calculation unit configured to, when the article to be handled by the robot is an unknown article whose shape is not registered in advance, calculate an operation of the robot for the unknown article by deforming the basic operation data stored in the storage unit, based on the shape of the unknown article measured by the shape measurement unit and the known shape of the basic article corresponding to the basic operation data.

[0007] According to this configuration, since the basic operation data prepared in advance for a known article is deformed in accordance with the measured shape of an unknown article, it is possible to generate, without new teaching, an operation of the robot suited to the unknown article, using the difference between the known shape and the measured shape of the unknown article.

---

## BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

[0008]
- **FIG. 1** is a block diagram showing a schematic configuration of a robot system according to an embodiment.
- **FIG. 2** is a diagram showing an example of a basic article and basic operation data stored in a storage unit.
- **FIG. 3** is a diagram showing an example of an unknown article and its measured shape.
- **FIG. 4** is a diagram illustrating a method of deforming basic operation data based on a difference between a basic shape and a measured shape.
- **FIG. 5** is a flowchart showing a processing procedure executed by an operation method calculation unit.
- **FIG. 6** is a diagram showing another example in which a plurality of pieces of basic operation data are selectively combined and deformed.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF EMBODIMENTS

### 1. Overall Configuration

[0009] FIG. 1 shows a schematic configuration of a robot system 1 according to the present embodiment. The robot system 1 includes a robot 10, a shape measurement unit 20, a storage unit 30, an operation method calculation unit 40, and a robot control unit 50.

[0010] The robot 10 includes a base, an arm having a plurality of joints, and an end effector (for example, a gripping hand, a suction pad, or the like) attached to a distal end of the arm. The robot 10 is configured to act on an article W, such as gripping, lifting, moving, and placing the article W, by driving the arm and the end effector in accordance with operation commands supplied from the robot control unit 50.

### 2. Shape Measurement Unit

[0011] The shape measurement unit 20 is configured to measure a three-dimensional shape of the article W to be handled by the robot 10. The shape measurement unit 20 may include, for example, a camera, a stereo camera, a laser range sensor, a time-of-flight (ToF) sensor, or a combination thereof, and outputs shape data representing the outer shape, dimensions, and/or a three-dimensional point cloud of the article W.

[0012] The shape measurement unit 20 may be attached to the arm of the robot 10 so as to measure the article W from a plurality of viewpoints, or may be installed at a fixed position, such as above a workbench, so as to measure the article W placed within a measurement region.

[0013] The shape data output from the shape measurement unit 20 is supplied to the operation method calculation unit 40, and is also used, when necessary, for the below-described determination of whether the article W is a known article or an unknown article.

### 3. Storage Unit

[0014] The storage unit 30 stores, in advance, basic shape data indicating shapes of one or more basic articles, and basic operation data indicating operations of the robot 10 for handling the respective basic articles. The basic operation data may be generated in advance by a teaching operation performed by an operator, or may be generated by simulation, and includes, for example, a gripping position, a gripping posture, an approach trajectory, a lifting trajectory, and a placement trajectory of the end effector with respect to the basic article.

[0015] As shown in FIG. 2, for example, the storage unit 30 may store basic shape data B1 representing a rectangular parallelepiped-shaped basic article having a width W1, a depth D1, and a height H1, in association with basic operation data M1 defining a gripping width, a gripping height position, and an approach direction of the end effector suited to the basic article.

[0016] The storage unit 30 may store a plurality of sets of basic shape data and basic operation data corresponding to a plurality of basic articles having mutually different shapes, such as a rectangular parallelepiped shape, a cylindrical shape, and a shape having a handle or a recessed grip portion.

### 4. Operation Method Calculation Unit

[0017] The operation method calculation unit 40 determines, based on the shape data measured by the shape measurement unit 20 and the basic shape data stored in the storage unit 30, whether the article W to be handled is a known article matching, within a predetermined tolerance, any of the basic articles stored in the storage unit 30, or an unknown article which does not match any of the basic articles.

[0018] When the article W is determined to be a known article, the operation method calculation unit 40 reads out the basic operation data corresponding to the matching basic article from the storage unit 30, and supplies the read-out basic operation data, without modification, to the robot control unit 50 as operation data for the robot 10.

[0019] On the other hand, when the article W is determined to be an unknown article, the operation method calculation unit 40 selects, from among the plurality of basic articles stored in the storage unit 30, at least one basic article having a shape similar to the measured shape of the unknown article, based on a predetermined similarity criterion, such as a shape category, a dimensional ratio, or a feature quantity of the shape.

[0020] The operation method calculation unit 40 then calculates a deformed operation, by deforming the basic operation data corresponding to the selected basic article, based on a difference between the known shape of the selected basic article and the measured shape of the unknown article.

[0021] As shown in FIG. 3 and FIG. 4, for example, when the unknown article W2 has a width W2, a depth D2, and a height H2 different from the width W1, depth D1, and height H1 of the basic article, the operation method calculation unit 40 may calculate a deformed gripping width by scaling the gripping width included in the basic operation data M1 in accordance with the ratio of the width W2 to the width W1, may calculate a deformed gripping height position by scaling the gripping height position in accordance with the ratio of the height H2 to the height H1, and may calculate a deformed approach trajectory by translating and/or rotating the approach direction included in the basic operation data M1 in accordance with a positional relationship between a reference point of the basic article and a reference point of the unknown article.

[0022] The deformation processing performed by the operation method calculation unit 40 is not limited to linear scaling, and may include, for example, non-linear deformation processing according to a difference in shape category (for example, deformation from a rectangular parallelepiped shape to a shape having a chamfered corner), interpolation processing using a plurality of pieces of basic operation data corresponding to a plurality of basic articles, and/or correction processing based on an estimated center-of-gravity position or an estimated weight of the unknown article W2.

[0023] As shown in FIG. 6, the operation method calculation unit 40 may select two or more basic articles similar to the unknown article, and may calculate the deformed operation by weighted interpolation of the plurality of pieces of basic operation data corresponding to the respective selected basic articles, using weighting coefficients determined in accordance with a degree of similarity between the shape of the unknown article and the respective shapes of the selected basic articles.

[0024] The deformed operation calculated by the operation method calculation unit 40 is supplied to the robot control unit 50 as the operation data for the robot 10.

### 5. Robot Control Unit

[0025] The robot control unit 50 generates operation commands for driving the arm and the end effector of the robot 10, based on the operation data supplied from the operation method calculation unit 40, and thereby causes the robot 10 to execute a series of operations, such as approaching, gripping, lifting, conveying, and placing the article W.

### 6. Processing Flow

[0026] FIG. 5 is a flowchart showing an example of a processing procedure executed by the operation method calculation unit 40.

- **Step S1:** The shape measurement unit 20 measures the shape of the article W to be handled.
- **Step S2:** The operation method calculation unit 40 compares the measured shape with the basic shape data stored in the storage unit 30, and determines whether the article W is a known article or an unknown article.
- **Step S3:** When the article W is a known article (Yes in S2), the operation method calculation unit 40 reads out the corresponding basic operation data, and the process proceeds to Step S6.
- **Step S4:** When the article W is an unknown article (No in S2), the operation method calculation unit 40 selects at least one basic article similar to the unknown article.
- **Step S5:** The operation method calculation unit 40 calculates the deformed operation by deforming the basic operation data corresponding to the selected basic article, based on the difference between the shape of the selected basic article and the measured shape of the unknown article.
- **Step S6:** The robot control unit 50 causes the robot 10 to execute the operation, based on the basic operation data or the deformed operation.

### 7. Modified Examples

[0027] Although the above embodiment describes an example in which the shape measurement unit 20 measures the shape of the article W prior to the operation of the robot 10, the shape measurement unit 20 may be configured to measure the shape of the article W repeatedly or continuously during the operation of the robot 10, and the operation method calculation

# Patent Application Summary

## Title
**System and Method for Generalizing Learned Robotic Grasping Motions to Novel Objects Based on Shape Similarity**

## Field of the Invention
This invention relates to robotic manipulation systems, and more particularly to methods for transferring previously learned grasping strategies to new, previously unseen objects by leveraging geometric and topological shape similarity analysis.

## Background
Conventional robotic grasping systems typically require either (1) extensive training on large datasets covering diverse object categories, or (2) object-specific programming for each new item encountered. These approaches suffer from poor scalability when robots encounter novel objects in unstructured environments, such as warehouses, homes, or manufacturing floors with variable inventory. Existing solutions often fail to leverage the inherent shape similarities between previously encountered objects and new ones, resulting in inefficient re-learning processes or grasp failures.

## Summary of the Invention

The disclosed system provides a robotic manipulation architecture comprising:

**1. Shape Representation Module**
- Converts sensor data (RGB-D, point cloud, or LIDAR input) of both training objects and novel target objects into a normalized geometric descriptor format
- Utilizes a learned embedding space that captures shape features relevant to graspability (curvature, symmetry, aspect ratio, surface topology)

**2. Grasp Motion Library**
- Stores a database of successful grasping trajectories, associated with the shape embeddings of objects on which they were originally learned
- Each entry includes approach vector, hand/gripper pose sequence, force profiles, and contact point configurations

**3. Similarity Matching Engine**
- Computes similarity scores between a novel object's shape embedding and stored embeddings using a distance metric in the learned feature space
- Identifies one or more candidate reference grasps from the library based on shape correspondence rather than object class/identity

**4. Motion Adaptation Module**
- Applies a transformation function to warp the reference grasp trajectory to accommodate geometric differences between the reference and novel object (scale, local curvature deviations, orientation)
- Incorporates real-time sensor feedback to refine the adapted trajectory during execution

**5. Execution and Feedback Loop**
- Executes the adapted grasp with continuous monitoring of force/tactile sensors
- Updates the grasp motion library with new successful executions, enabling incremental learning without full retraining

## Key Advantages
- Enables **few-shot or zero-shot grasping** of novel objects using shape analogy rather than exhaustive training
- Reduces computational and data requirements compared to end-to-end deep learning approaches trained per-object
- Supports **continuous learning** through library expansion during deployment
- Applicable across manipulator types (parallel-jaw grippers, multi-fingered hands, suction end-effectors)

## Potential Claims Focus Areas
1. Method for shape-based grasp transfer using embedding similarity
2. System architecture integrating shape encoder, motion library, and adaptation module
3. Trajectory warping algorithm based on geometric correspondence
4. Incremental library update mechanism based on execution outcomes
5. Multi-modal sensor fusion for shape descriptor generation

---

**Note:** This is a template/starting point. A licensed patent attorney should review claims for novelty against prior art (e.g., existing grasp transfer learning patents from Google, Berkeley robotics labs, etc.) and ensure proper legal claim structuring before filing.

# SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to a robot system, and more particularly, to a robot system capable of automatically calculating an operation method suitable for a workpiece shape based on measured shape data, thereby improving operational efficiency and versatility across varying workpiece configurations.

According to an aspect of the present invention, there is provided a robot system comprising: a mechanism unit configured to perform a predetermined operation on a workpiece; a shape measurement unit configured to measure a shape of the workpiece and generate shape data representing the measured shape; a basic operation storage unit configured to store a plurality of basic operations executable by the mechanism unit; an operation method calculation unit configured to calculate an operation method for the mechanism unit based on the shape data generated by the shape measurement unit and the plurality of basic operations stored in the basic operation storage unit; and a control unit configured to control the mechanism unit so as to execute the operation method calculated by the operation method calculation unit.

In an embodiment, the shape measurement unit may include at least one sensor selected from the group consisting of a camera, a laser displacement sensor, a three-dimensional scanner, and a distance measurement sensor, and may be configured to generate the shape data as three-dimensional coordinate data or point cloud data representing an outer shape of the workpiece.

In an embodiment, the basic operation storage unit may store, as the plurality of basic operations, a plurality of operation patterns each associated with a corresponding basic shape, and the operation method calculation unit may be configured to select at least one of the plurality of operation patterns based on a result of comparison between the shape data and the basic shapes associated with the plurality of operation patterns, and to combine the selected operation patterns to calculate the operation method.

In an embodiment, the operation method calculation unit may be configured to divide the shape indicated by the shape data into a plurality of partial regions, select, for each of the plurality of partial regions, a basic operation corresponding to a shape of the partial region from among the plurality of basic operations, and calculate the operation method by combining the basic operations selected for the plurality of partial regions in a predetermined order.

In an embodiment, the operation method calculation unit may be configured to calculate at least one of a movement path, a movement speed, and a posture of the mechanism unit as the operation method, based on the shape data.

In an embodiment, the robot system may further comprise a determination unit configured to determine whether or not a basic operation corresponding to the shape data is stored in the basic operation storage unit, wherein, when the determination unit determines that no basic operation corresponding to the shape data is stored, the operation method calculation unit is configured to generate a new operation method by correcting or combining at least one of the plurality of basic operations stored in the basic operation storage unit.

In an embodiment, the robot system may further comprise a storage control unit configured to store, in the basic operation storage unit, the operation method calculated by the operation method calculation unit in association with the shape data, as a new basic operation.

In an embodiment, the mechanism unit may include an arm portion having a plurality of joints, and an end effector provided at a distal end of the arm portion, and the control unit may be configured to control at least one of the plurality of joints and the end effector in accordance with the operation method calculated by the operation method calculation unit.

According to the robot system of the present invention configured as described above, since the operation method suited to the shape of the workpiece is automatically calculated based on the basic operations stored in advance and the shape data obtained by measurement, it becomes possible to cause the mechanism unit to execute an appropriate operation without requiring an operator to individually teach an operation for every workpiece shape. As a result, the time and labor required for teaching operations can be significantly reduced, and the robot system can flexibly accommodate workpieces of a wide variety of shapes, thereby achieving both improved operational accuracy and enhanced versatility.

Furthermore, by accumulating newly calculated operation methods as basic operations, the robot system can progressively expand the repertoire of basic operations stored in the basic operation storage unit, so that the accuracy and efficiency of the operation method calculation can be further improved through repeated use of the system.

# Abstract

**Title:** Generalized Robotic Grasping via Few-Shot Shape-Based Object Registration

This paper presents a robotic manipulation system capable of handling a wide variety of articles using only a small number of pre-registered example objects, with generalization to previously unseen items that share similar geometric characteristics. Conventional robotic picking systems typically require extensive training datasets or exhaustive object-specific models to achieve reliable grasp planning, limiting their scalability in dynamic environments such as warehouses, retail fulfillment centers, and flexible manufacturing lines. To address this limitation, the proposed system employs a shape-based feature extraction and matching framework that enables generalization from a minimal set of registered exemplars—typically three to five representative shapes—to a broad class of morphologically similar objects.

The system architecture comprises three primary modules: (1) a 3D perception module utilizing depth sensing and point cloud reconstruction to capture the geometric profile of target articles, (2) a shape descriptor module that encodes rotation- and scale-invariant features via a combination of principal component analysis and learned embeddings from a lightweight convolutional network, and (3) a grasp planning module that retrieves the nearest-matching registered template and adapts grasp parameters—including approach vector, gripper aperture, and contact force—according to the estimated shape correspondence and surface curvature of the novel object.

Registration of new object categories requires only a brief manual demonstration phase, during which a small number of representative samples are scanned and annotated with successful grasp configurations. During runtime, unknown objects are classified against this compact template library using a similarity metric based on geometric moment invariants and surface normal histograms, allowing the system to infer suitable grasping strategies without requiring category-specific retraining.

Experimental validation was conducted on a 6-degree-of-freedom robotic arm equipped with an adaptive parallel-jaw gripper, tested across a dataset of over 150 household and industrial articles spanning categories such as boxes, cylindrical containers, irregular packaging, and soft deformable items. Results demonstrate a grasp success rate exceeding 89% for objects not included in the original registration set, provided they exhibit shape similarity to at least one registered template, with average grasp planning latency under 200 milliseconds. Comparative analysis against conventional deep-learning-based grasp detection methods trained on large-scale datasets indicates comparable performance despite a substantial reduction in required training data and computational overhead.

These findings suggest that shape-similarity-based few-shot registration offers a practical and scalable alternative to data-intensive learning approaches for robotic grasping, particularly in applications where rapid deployment and adaptability to novel inventory are critical. Future work will explore integration with tactile feedback and dynamic re-registration to further improve robustness in cluttered and unstructured environments.

**Keywords:** robotic grasping, few-shot learning, shape matching, grasp planning, object generalization, point cloud registration
